target.title: Dashboard: stateful notes widget — the first consumer of widget write-back
target.body:
> 📦 **Part of the modular-dashboard package** — master hub **#101136** (architecture diagrams · bottom-up merge order · the full per-PR test map).
>
> 🧪 **Try this PR:** add the `notes` builtin, edit it, and reload → stateful markdown/todo persists (rides write-back #101329).

---

> A notes pad on your dashboard that actually saves — and the pattern every stateful builtin after it will follow.

Closes #101146. **Stacked on #101329 (widget write-back)**, which is itself stacked on #101098 — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review `notes.ts` + the `buildBuiltinContext` host change as the delta beyond #101329.

## What's in this PR

- **`builtin:notes`** — an editable notes/todo pad. Content hydrates from persisted state on mount and saves on debounced input (~500 ms), so it survives reloads and stays consistent across two open browsers (the write-back broadcast triggers refetch).
- **A host-bound state accessor for builtins** — the piece that makes this safe and reusable. `BuiltinWidgetContext` gains an optional `state` accessor (`get`/`set`), and the dashboard view now builds the context **per widget** (`buildBuiltinContext`), closing over the host's own `widget.id` when it calls `dashboard.widget.state.get`/`.set`. A widget renderer never names a widget id — it can only ever touch its own state. This mirrors the trust model of the sandboxed path in #101329 (parent binds the id), applied to trusted builtins.
- **Graceful degradation** — with no connected client there's no `state` accessor, and the pad renders read-only with a hint instead of silently dropping writes.

## How it works
Builtins render in the trusted Control UI, so they use the write-back gateway RPCs directly rather than the sandbox's postMessage bridge — but the id-binding discipline is identical: the host supplies `widget.id`, never the renderer. The persist test drives the real `buildBuiltinContext` (not a hand-rolled mock) and asserts the RPC receives `{ widgetId: "notes-42", state: … }` — the id-binding itself is under test. State lives in the per-widget jailed store from #101329 (64 KB cap, atomic writes, separate from `workspace.json`).

No new dependency — `pnpm-lock.yaml` unchanged.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** Operators want a scratchpad/todo on their dashboard, but before write-back (#101137/#101329) any editable widget reset on reload — and there was no pattern for a *builtin* to persist state safely. This adds a stateful notes builtin plus the host-bound per-widget state accessor that makes it (and future stateful builtins) possible.
**Evidence:** `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard` → 98 passed, including the four new notes cases (editable render, hydrate from mocked `state.get`, debounced persist through the real host-built context asserting the host-bound `widget.id`, and the read-only no-client fallback); `pnpm ui:i18n:check` clean; `pnpm ui:build` and full type-aware oxlint clean.
